-122.32400,47.60920.name: Pacific Northwest Fertility and IVF Specialists
-122.32400,47.60920.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Julie D. Lamb, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-79.81000,35.63000.name: Durham VA Medical Center
-79.81000,35.63000.type: Animal Welfare Act veterans affairs hospital
-79.81000,35.63000.desc: Veterans Affairs hospital registered with USDA APHIS under the Animal Welfare Act, certificate 55-V-0003. This is the address on the registration. A research registration is issued to an organisation rather than to a building, so for a university it is usually the research administration office and the animals are elsewhere on campus or in another city. Rats, mice and birds bred for research are excluded from the Act's definition of an animal — the overwhelming majority of animals used, and the great majority of the genetically altered ones. What is covered here is dogs, cats, primates, rabbits, guinea pigs, hamsters and farm animals. The rest is counted nowhere.

-72.48317,45.89534.name: Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières
-72.48317,45.89534.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, May 2024
-72.48317,45.89534.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, May 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-73.05021,-36.82707.name: IMR- Instituto de Medicina Reproductiva
-73.05021,-36.82707.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: https://imr.cl/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere. No street address resolved, so this point is the city or the country rather than the centre.

0.18300,52.07700.name: Cyagen / knockout mouse repositories — IMPC
0.18300,52.07700.desc: The International Mouse Phenotyping Consortium is systematically knocking out every protein-coding gene in the mouse and recording what happens, roughly twenty thousand genes across a network of centres. It is the largest deliberate programme of animal genetic modification ever undertaken, run by public institutions, and its output is a catalogue any laboratory can order from.

7.09800,50.73400.name: IFOAM — Organics International
7.09800,50.73400.desc: The global umbrella for organic standards, which exclude genetic engineering by definition in every member scheme. It is the largest coordinated market structure anywhere built around the absence of this technology, and it sets the terms on which coexistence is argued.

11.58200,48.14100.name: Max Planck Society
11.58200,48.14100.desc: Germany's principal basic research organisation, and where Charpentier ran the unit that produced her share of the CRISPR patents. Institutes of this kind hold the intellectual property their researchers generate, so a public research body becomes a licensor whether or not it set out to be one.

-90.00000,37.21000.name: Bader Farms, Inc. v. Monsanto Company and BASF Corporation
-90.00000,37.21000.state: Cape Girardeau — US District Court, Eastern District of Missouri
-90.00000,37.21000.desc: Missouri's largest peach farm sued over dicamba drift, and in February 2020 a jury awarded $15 million in compensatory and $250 million in punitive damages — the first US jury verdict for property damage to a neighbouring landowner from dicamba drift. The punitive award was reduced to $60 million later that year, and in July 2022 the Eighth Circuit upheld liability while ordering a new trial on punitive damages. The claim was not about the herbicide alone. It was that dicamba-tolerant soybean and cotton seed had been released knowing the accompanying herbicide would move off target onto crops that could not tolerate it. The farm's harvest fell from around 162,000 bushels in the early 2000s to as low as 12,000 in 2018, and it said it would inevitably close. The companies denied the allegations and attributed the damage to illegal applications by other farmers, weather and disease. However that dispute is resolved, the structure is what this map should record: a tolerance trait creates a market for the matching herbicide, and the cost of it landing elsewhere falls on whoever did not buy either.

57.55000,-20.48000.name: Bioculture Group
57.55000,-20.48000.desc: Founded in 1985 and now, on its own account, a world leader in the breeding and export of specific-pathogen-free long-tailed macaques. In 2021 it and a few other Mauritian firms exported an average of around 14,000 macaques a year, and 70 per cent of Mauritian macaques reaching the United States that year came from this company. The reason for that share is entirely traceable on this map: China exported roughly 30,000 of the species in 2018 and closed the tap during the pandemic to supply its own biomedical sector; Cambodia filled the gap until the 2022 indictment; Mauritius, Vietnam and Indonesia then absorbed the demand. Its own materials emphasise pathogen screening, genetic profiling and pedigree tracking — the traceability the Cambodian prosecution showed was missing elsewhere.
